newsitem.title: GERMANY: Time right for Allianz takeover of AGF-Merck Finck.
newsitem.headline: Time right for Allianz takeover of AGF-Merck Finck.

text.p: The time may be right for German insurer Allianz AG Holding to take over Assurances Generales de France (AGF), as has been repeatedly rumoured, analysts at Merck, Finck & Co said on Thursday.
"According to (our) assessment, Allianz has been trying for years to get a stronger hold on the French market," the Munich-based bank said in a statement.

"The timing to buy Europe's eighth largest insurance company is favourable considering the value, expected earnings development and current share price," it said, adding that the chance of a move made Allianz a short term "speculative buy".
Allianz refuses to comment on such speculation while AGF has noted that it was not in the German giant's tradition to embark on an unfriendly takeover.

Other analysts have played down the likelihood of such a takeover, arguing that this might complicate Allianz' position on the German market because of AGF's close connections with Aachener Muenchener Beteiligungs AG.

Allianz, which already dominates German insurance, last year had to sell its Deutsche Krankenversicherungs AG health insurance unit to ease German cartel office concerns about its potential monopoly in this insurance segment.
Merck Finck also said it expected major changes on the German insurance market, which is currently wrestling with deregulation, globalisation and sharp price competition.
German insurers' favoured strategy would likely be taking stakes in foreign companies and gradually building up to takeovers, the bank predicted.

Speculation earlier this month that Allianz might be interested in AGF was triggered by a report in the French press about possible shake-ups in the insurance sector after the multi-billion dollar takeover by French insurer Axa of competitor UAP last year.
The daily Le Monde reported earlier this month that Dominique Bazy, one of the top executives from Axa/UAP, had left the company to head up Allianz's French unit.
That followed Allianz's decision in January to take full control of its French subsidiary Allianz Via Holding France, ending years of legal strife with its former French partner over the venture.
